terms.gloss: sailor; in the plural, the crew
evidence: Caes. BG 3.9: nautās gubernātōrēsque comparārī jubet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin names a crew by what its men are: the sailors, nautae, or the rowers.

terms.gloss: the rowers, the crew of oarsmen
terms.comment: First the rowing, then the oars, and collectively the oarsmen (Cic. Tusc. 5.114; Liv.); Traupman gives it for a rowing crew. For an air crew see steward; for a crew of workers, team.

phrases.english: he orders sailors and helmsmen to be got together

sources: Lewis & Short: nauta · Lewis & Short: remigium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 49.
